gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, at today's maker price, the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 ($499 at bluettipower.com, 890 Wh measured usable by OutdoorGearLab) costs $0.56 per usable watt-hour. That is the lowest of any 1 kWh camping station with a measured capacity. The Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 that ChatGPT showed at $699.99 is $529.99 on Amazon today ($0.60), and the EcoFlow DELTA 3 is $579 ($0.67).
standout_why: I compared against the two cited pages. OutdoorGearLab (2026-07-23) measured usable Wh but prices models at old list prices: Elite 100 V2 $799, C1000 Gen 2 $799, DELTA 3 $699. It ranks the Elite 100 V2 9th and never works out cost per usable Wh. GearJunkie (2026-10-31) gives only a rough '$1 per Wh' rule and a '25% less than rated' rule, with no measured usable Wh, and it doesn't review the Elite 100 V2. ChatGPT's own cards show the C1000 Gen 2 at $699.99 and the Explorer 1000 v2 at $499. No page puts today's prices together with measured usable capacity.
decides: Price confirms the 1 kWh class as the car-camping pick, but it shifts value at today's prices. The Elite 100 V2 (our product) gives the most usable Wh per dollar: $0.56 against $0.60 for the C1000 Gen 2. It loses to the C1000 Gen 2 only on recharge speed, 2.0 h against 0.9 h on OutdoorGearLab's wall-charge test. The C1000 Gen 2 is still the pick for anyone who recharges between campsites, but ChatGPT's $699.99 card overstates its price by $170. For phones and lights only, the BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 at $289.99 (288 Wh) is one cent more than the Jackery Explorer 300 at $289. The Explorer 300 is the measured small unit at $1.11 per usable Wh.
